rows.name: TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL

cells.Set by: The Nix lint shell and the Nix `lefthook` wrapper (`flake.nix`).
cells.Values and default: Only the exact text `1` turns it on. Any other text counts as off. Unset: off. The hook commands try `ci/.venv/bin/ruff` and `ci/.venv/bin/python` first, then the tools on `PATH`.
cells.Effect: With `1`, the Lefthook (Git hook runner) commands `ruff-format`, `ruff-check` and `agent-guidance` run `ruff` and `python3` from `PATH` and do not look in `ci/.venv/bin`. `bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh` does the same for `python3`. A missing `ruff` or `nixfmt` then fails the hook command. `flake.nix` sets `1` in the Nix lint shell (`nix develop .#lint`, `x86_64-linux` only) and in the `lefthook` wrapper of the Nix dev shell. `bin/ci/test-nix-lint-toolchain.sh` fails without `1`. Without `1`, a missing `ruff` or `nixfmt` is skipped when `CI` is unset or empty.

rows.name: pci_id

cells.Values and default: Text of the form `vvvv:dddd`: a PCI vendor ID of 4 hex digits, a colon, and a device ID of 4 hex digits. The script passes it unquoted to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh`. Unset: `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` gets only the card address. It prints a warning and continues without the ID check.
cells.Effect: Unless its first argument is `unbind`, `bin/bind-cards.sh` passes the value to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` for each FPGA card. That script checks for a device with this vendor and device ID at the card address, then binds the card to `vfio-pci` (the Linux driver for user-space PCI access). A mismatch stops both scripts. The script takes `pci_id` from its environment and never assigns it. It prints the value in each `binding` line. The `unbind` mode does not use it. Text in another form, such as `8200:`, stops the script. Text in PCI address form replaces the card address.

rows.name: start_address

cells.Values and default: Offset from the base address, as hexadecimal digits without the `0x` prefix. The script adds `0x` in front and uses the text in bash arithmetic without a check. Unset: the offset counts as 0. The first address is the base address `0x37000000000`.
cells.Effect: `bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh` uses `start_address` before it assigns it. On the first pass of its loop it adds the inherited value to the base address `0x37000000000`. It writes a test pattern to that memory address with `./iotools mmio_write64` and reads it back. Each later pass adds the address of the previous pass to the base address again. The script reads the address range of each line of `address_map_1.csv` into `range` and never uses it. It runs `./iotools` from the current directory.

rows.name: CLIFF_BYSTANDERS

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A value above the maximum is lowered to the maximum. Unset: the test case uses the maximum. Empty: counts as `0`, and the test case skips.
cells.Effect: Sets the largest number of bystander threads (extra waiting threads) that the test case `spin waiter storm at scale (56c cliff)` starts. Smaller rounds with 4, 8, 16 and 32 threads still run when they are not above this number. A result below 8 threads makes the test case skip. The maximum is the number of application CPUs (CPU cores that the process pins its application threads to) minus 3, and at most 53 threads. `0` and negative values cause the skip. The skip message reports too few application CPUs, also when the variable causes the skip.

rows.name: HWALLOC_STRESS

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `std::stoi`. Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stoi` throw an exception when the test run starts. Unset: `1`. Empty: `std::stoi` throws an exception when the test run starts.

rows.name: PAUSE_HINT

cells.Values and default: `0` or `1`, parsed with `std::stoi`. The test output labels `1` as `C0.1` and `0` as `C0.2` (two low-power wait states of Intel CPUs). Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stoi` throw an exception. The test case then fails. Unset: `1`. Empty: `std::stoi` throws an exception.
cells.Effect: Sets the hint argument of the CPU instruction `tpause` in the spin-wait benchmark (a test loop that polls a shared variable and does not sleep). The main thread and the worker thread both use it. Read only when `PAUSE_TYPE` is `tpause`. The test requires a value of at most `1`. The test stores the value in 8 bits before that check. `256` becomes `0` and passes. `-1` becomes `255` and fails.

unresolved: start_address - whether a bash newer than 5.1 still reads `0x` with no digits as 0. The row says that an unset variable gives the base address on the first pass. A standalone snippet with the arithmetic line of bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh:15 confirmed this on bash 5.1.16 only. Running `bash -c 'echo $((0x))'` on a lab host with a newer bash settles it.
notes: Short version: all 12 rows agree with the code at commit 7eddde7895, so every verdict is `correct`. 5 rows changed, and only for house rules. 7 rows are unchanged. Changes: UV - the row had 1,119 characters and now has 995. The file count in `Read by` became `and other files`. The counts of `bin/ci` scripts are gone. The empty-value facts now stand once, in `Values and default`. The two CI sentences became one. MIXTRAL_PATH - the row had 1,025 characters and now has 992. All counts of files, tests and test programs are gone. The Rust test that prints a skip message is named. Two sentences that repeated `Values and default` were removed to fit the limit. CLIFF_BYSTANDERS - the quoted skip message (a test text in section 4, rule 7) became plain words. HWALLOC_STRESS - `Six test cases` became `The stress test cases` (rule 5). PAUSE_HINT - the hint about `C0.1` and `C0.2` is applied with the clause `two low-power wait states of Intel CPUs`. The mapping of 1 and 0 to the two names is in t/t_mwaitx.cpp:757. The meaning of the names comes from the Intel description of the `tpause` instruction, not from Tron code. The other terms in that hint belong to other rows. The same cell now has an `Empty:` case and says that the test case fails after the exception. An empty value makes `std::stoi` throw, and an unset value gives 1 (t/t_mwaitx.cpp:739). In `Effect`, `polls a flag` became `polls a shared variable`. The validator rejects the word `flag`, and the sibling rows PAUSE_LEN_NS and PAUSE_TYPE in audit2/13.json use the same new wording. Observations for the document owner: (1) HWALLOC_STRESS and PAUSE_HINT use `std::stoi`, and the list of parse functions in `Words used here` has no `stoi`. (2) HWALLOC_STRESS: the row says that `std::stoi` throws when the test run starts. What the test program prints and returns after that depends on Catch2, whose source is not in the checkout, so the row does not state it. (3) The validator does not find a number word such as `Six test cases`. Method: only reads of the checkout (git grep, sed -n, Read). One standalone bash snippet outside the checkout measured the arithmetic of `0x` plus an unset variable for start_address. One shell command used `cd` into the scratchpad directory by mistake. It did not touch the checkout. The checkout index holds staged changes that are not part of commit 7eddde7895 (README.env-vars.md added, AGENTS.md and README.md modified). They were excluded from every search.
